open-question.question: Over which runs is the field measurement of the completion procedure's read of past work taken: which projects and hosts, starting from which plugin release, and how many completion runs at the least before its result is read?
open-question.applied-principle: Check tier claims against the live environment
open-question.recommendation: The read is meant for field projects whose files are code, which this repository's prose-heavy, invariant-documented tasks cannot stand in for, and other projects on this machine already hold completion runs in the same transcript store both earlier measurements read; about 200 runs combined matches the 202-transcript completion sample and leaves enough counted runs to read a share, reachable in weeks at this repository's 141 task commits over the last month plus the other projects once a release ships, while a reader per host and a pre-landing baseline add work the result does not use.
open-question.alternative: Projects: this repository plus every other project on this machine running the plugin, as the 88-run answer-sweep measurement of 2026-10-18 spanned seven projects. Hosts: Claude Code only. Start: the landing commit for this repository and, for every other project, the first release that ships this milestone's procedure change (the next after 1.9.0), since those projects install from the distribution repository; no pre-landing baseline. Minimum: on the order of 200 completion runs across the projects combined. Field projects whose files are code rather than plugin prose enter the sample, which is the population the discretionary read is meant to serve, while the sample stays in the one transcript format both earlier field measurements were taken from. The other projects contribute nothing until a release ships and they upgrade, and they hold few or no task commits carrying a bar (a bar stands in the commit body only from milestone 53 on), so many of their runs meet a read that prints little; how many of the combined runs count at all is the run-population question's to decide.

Projects: this repository only. Hosts: Claude Code only, read from its local session transcripts. Start: the commit that lands the rebuilt `hosts/claude/` tree carrying the read, since the maintainer's directory marketplace serves `./hosts/claude` and so runs it before any release; no pre-landing baseline. Minimum: a few tens of completion runs, on the order of 30, before the result is read. The result arrives soonest and from the one project whose task commits carry verified bars and whose files have the deepest task history, so the read has something to surface: this repository landed 141 `Task-completion:` commits over nine active days in the month to 2026-11-10, which puts 30 runs a few working days after the landing. One self-dogfooding project's agents edit mostly plugin prose whose shape `CLAUDE.md`'s invariants already explain, so a few tens of its runs can say little about field projects and leave a low but real rate of skipped or hand-rolled reads unseen; a small sample only settles the question under a sibling rule that a single failing run is enough, which is the result rule's to decide.

Projects: this repository only. Hosts: Claude Code only. Start: the commit that lands the rebuilt `hosts/claude/` tree carrying the read; no pre-landing baseline. Minimum: on the order of 200 completion runs, the size of the 202-transcript completion-agent sample milestone 46 measured on 2026-10-08. A sample the size of the one an earlier completion-procedure decision already rested on, all on the plugin version as built in this tree and in transcripts at hand, so a share-based result rule can be read with the confidence that decision had, with no dependence on other projects upgrading. At this repository's recent pace it takes weeks of milestones to reach, the read staying discretionary all the while, and the sample stays one project's, so it measures how agents behave on this repository's prose-heavy files, not whether field agents on code projects take the read.

Projects: this repository plus every other project on this machine running the plugin. Hosts: all three, Claude Code, Antigravity, and Codex, each read from its own session store and reported per host. Start: the landing commit for this repository and the first release shipping the change (the next after 1.9.0) elsewhere; no pre-landing baseline. Minimum: on the order of 200 completion runs combined, every host's runs counted toward it. The procedure's prose reaches all three hosts but their agents differ (Codex runs its generic subagent told to read the agent file), so this is the only run set that can show a host whose agents never take the read or always hand-roll it, which a Claude-only sample would hide. Each host's transcripts come in their own format, so the measurement needs a reader per host (the host suite's `host.records` shape covers suite runs, not field session stores), and Antigravity and Codex completion runs are likely few, so their per-host figures may stay too small to read.

Projects: this repository plus every other project on this machine running the plugin. Hosts: Claude Code only. Start: the landing commit for this repository and the first release shipping the change elsewhere; no pre-landing baseline. Minimum: no run count; the run set is every completion run made until a fixed number of milestones, on the order of three, have finished in this repository after the landing, and the result is read then. It matches the design draft's own framing, that the read's question is answered by field runs over the milestones that follow, and it ends at a point the plan can name in advance, so the measurement cannot stall waiting on a count. The number of runs it yields is unknown when the plan is written (three milestones may hold a dozen tasks or fifty), so a share-based result may rest on too few runs to read, and the window says nothing about how much the other projects contribute.

Projects: this repository plus every other project on this machine running the plugin. Hosts: Claude Code only. Start: two windows, a baseline of the completion runs already in the transcripts from 2026-10-30, when milestone 53 created the `tasks` query, up to the landing, when agents could have read the record but were not told to; and the measured window from the landing commit here and the first release shipping the change elsewhere. Minimum: on the order of 200 completion runs in the measured window, the baseline taken whole whatever it holds. The baseline is available at once from transcripts already on disk and shows how often agents composed their own `git log`, `git blame`, or `git show` before the procedure named the command, so the measured window's figures read as a change against that rate rather than as a bare number. The baseline spans a different procedure and a mix of plugin versions, so it adds a second set to read and classify for a comparison the result rule may not use, and it inherits the measured window's wait on other projects upgrading; which outcomes are told apart in either window is the read-outcomes question's to decide.
